_comment: Operator-harness tunables for the Gate F run (tools/gate_f/operator_harness.gd). Deliberately NOT under data/config/: nothing the game ships reads this file, and ralph/GATE_F_INSTRUMENTATION_REQUEST.md section 10 forbids touching the game's data configs. Delete the file and the harness runs on the same values, hard-coded as defaults, so a bare checkout still works.
_comment_trace_hz: route.csv sample rate. The protocol section C.2 fixes it at 2 Hz for the run that produces Gate F evidence; the key is here so a diagnostic rerun can raise it without a code edit. Raising it costs frame time -- measure with --gatef-mode=overhead and record the result rather than assuming it is free.
_comment_settle_frames: Physics frames waited after a scene boot before anything is read or pressed. 240 is what every smoke test in tests/ uses; the Meadows scatters ~130k props at stand-up and a shorter settle reads half-built terrain as a defect.
_comment_walk_budget_frames: Physics frames one move_to step may spend walking before it reports FAIL. 2400 is 40 seconds at 60 Hz. Frames spent unable to move -- a fight, a fade, a conversation -- do not count against it (stick_navigator.gd's own rule), so this is a budget on WALKING, not on wall clock.
_comment_walk_close_enough: Metres from a move_to target that count as arrived. Looser than the navigator's own 0.8 default because a Gate F anchor is a place to stand, not a switch to press.
_comment_walk_held_budget_frames: Physics frames a move_to step will wait, in total, for locomotion to come back before giving up. 3600 is a minute at 60 Hz. stick_navigator.gd's own limit is ten minutes and then false; a harness cannot afford that, because a walk that hangs produces no evidence at all -- worse than one that reports where it stopped and what was holding it. Measured on main: walking out of the spawn triggers Grandpa's opening conversation, which takes locomotion and holds it until somebody answers.
_comment_perf_window_frames: Trailing window the perf field's avg/p95/max are computed over. 60 frames is one second at the physics rate, which is the shortest window a p95 means anything over.
_comment_capture_settle_frames: Process frames waited before a capture, on top of the frame_post_draw await. A capture taken on the frame a panel opens catches it mid-fade.
_comment_overhead_seconds: Length of each half of the section 8 overhead self-measurement (once with telemetry on, once off). 60 s each, per the request's own wording.
